Main.sentence: Bobby Lee Rush (born November 23, 1946) is an American politician, activist, and pastor who served as the ___E:U.S. representative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._representative)___ for Illinois's 1st congressional district for three decades, ending in 2023. A civil rights activist during the 1960s, Rush co-founded the Illinois chapter of the ___E:Black Panther Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Panther_Party)___ .
Rush was first elected to Congress in 1992. He won consecutive reelections until his retirement.

His district was originally principally on the ___E:South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side_(Chicago))___ of ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , with a population from 2003 to early 2013 that was 65% ___E:African-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American)___ , a higher proportion than any other ___E:congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_district)___ .
In 2011 the ___E:Illinois General Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_General_Assembly)___ redistricted this area after the 2010 census.
Although still ___E:minority-majority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minority-majority)___ , since early 2013 it is 51.3% African American, 36.1% White, 9.8% Hispanic, and 2% Asian.

A member of the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , Rush is the only politician to have defeated ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ in an election, which he did in the ___E:2000 Democratic primary for Illinois's 1st congressional district U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Illinois%27s_1st_congressional_district_election)___ .
On January 3, 2022, Rush announced that he was retiring from Congress.
Rush was born on November 23, 1946, in ___E:Albany, Georgia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albany,_Georgia)___ .

After his parents separated when Rush was 7 years old, his mother took him and his siblings to ___E:Chicago, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago,_Illinois)___ , joining the ___E:Great Migration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American))___ of African Americans out of the South in the first part of the 20th century.
In 1963, Rush dropped out of high school before graduating and joined the ___E:U.S. Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army)___ .

While stationed in Chicago in 1966, he joined the ___E:Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student_Nonviolent_Coordinating_Committee)___ , which had helped obtain national civil rights legislation passed in 1964 and 1965. In 1968, he went ___E:AWOL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AWOL)___ from the Army and co-founded the Illinois chapter of the ___E:Black Panthers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Panthers)___ .
He later finished his Army service, receiving an honorable discharge.

Throughout the 1960s, Rush was involved in the ___E:civil rights movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_rights_movement)___ and worked in civil disobedience campaigns in the ___E:southern United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States)___ .
After co-founding the Illinois chapter of the ___E:Black Panther Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Panther_Party)___ in 1968, he served as its defense minister.

After the Chicago Police Department and the State's Attorney Office assassinated Black Panther ___E:Fred Hampton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Hampton)___ in a police raid, Rush said, "We needed to arm ourselves", and called the police "pigs".
Earlier that year, Rush had discussed the philosophy of his membership in the Black Panthers, saying, "Black people have been on the defensive for all these years.
The trend now is not to wait to be attacked.
We advocate offensive violence against the power structure."  After Hampton's death, Rush became acting chairman of the Illinois Black Panther Party.

He worked on several nonviolent projects that built support for the Black Panthers in African-American communities, such as coordinating a medical clinic which offered ___E:sickle-cell anemia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sickle-cell_anemia)___ testing on an unprecedented scale.
Rush was imprisoned for six months in 1972 on a weapons charge after carrying a pistol into a police station.
In 1974, he left the Black Panthers, who were already in decline. "We started glorifying thuggery and drugs", he told People .
A deeply religious born-again ___E:Christian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity)___ , Rush said, "I don't repudiate any of my involvement in the Panther party—it was part of my maturing."

Rush earned his ___E:Bachelor of General Studies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_General_Studies)___ with honors from ___E:Roosevelt University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_University)___ in 1973, and a ___E:Master's degree U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master%27s_degree)___ in ___E:political science U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_science)___ from ___E:University of Illinois at Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_at_Chicago)___ in 1974. He completed a degree in ___E:theological studies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theology)___ at ___E:McCormick Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCormick_Theological_Seminary)___ in 1998.  On May 13, 2017, Rush received a Doctorate of Humanities, honoris causa , from the ___E:Illinois Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Institute_of_Technology)___ (IIT) for his outstanding contributions to Chicago.

In 1975, Rush ran for a seat on the ___E:Chicago City Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_City_Council)___ , the first of several black militants to seek political office, [citation needed] and lost to incumbent alderman William Barnett, receiving 23% of the vote to Barnett's 55% and Larry S. Bullock's 21%.
He ran again in 1983 and won, alongside ___E:Harold Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Washington)___ 's victory as Chicago's first black mayor.
Rush supported Washington's coalition during the Council Wars that followed the 1983 election.

Rush's allies in the black-power movement abandoned the Democrats in the wake of the political turmoil that followed the sudden death of Washington in 1987, and formed their own political party, naming it after Washington.

Rush infuriated ___E:Harold Washington Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Washington_Party)___ leaders by spurning their candidates for local offices and sometimes backing white Democrats instead.
He worked with the Democrats and was rewarded with the deputy chairmanship of the state party.

After redistricting in 1992, Rush ran in Illinois's newly redrawn 1st congressional district, which included much of Chicago's South Side. The district had a high proportion of African-American residents; it has been represented by Black congressmen since 1929. Rush defeated incumbent U.S.

Representative ___E:Charles Hayes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_A._Hayes)___ and six other candidates in the Democratic ___E:primary election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partisan_primary)___ .

He won the general election with 83% of the vote.  (The 1st is so heavily Democratic that Rush had all but assured himself of a seat in Congress with his primary win.) The district has been in Democratic hands since 1935.

In the 2000 Democratic primary for the district, Rush was challenged by ___E:Illinois State Senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Senate)___ ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .

During the primary, Rush said, "Barack Obama went to ___E:Harvard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard)___ and became an educated fool. Barack is a person who read about the civil rights protests and thinks he knows all about it."
Rush claimed Obama was insufficiently rooted in Chicago's black neighborhoods to represent constituents' concerns.

Obama said Rush was a part of "a politics that is rooted in the past" and said he could build bridges with whites to get things done. But while Obama did well in his own ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ ___E:base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_(politics))___ , he did not get enough support from the surrounding black neighborhoods.
Starting with 10% name recognition, Obama eventually gained 30% of the vote, losing by more than 2 to 1 despite winning among white voters.
Rush won 61% of the vote,      and won the general election with 88% of the vote.

In ___E:1999 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_Chicago_mayoral_election)___ , Rush ran for ___E:mayor of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Chicago)___ , but lost to incumbent ___E:Richard M. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_M._Daley)___ , an ethnic ___E:Irish American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_American)___ whose father had long controlled the city as mayor.
He remained active in city and regional politics.
In 2013, Rush criticized U.S.

Senator ___E:Mark Kirk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Kirk)___ 's proposal that 18,000 members of the Chicago gang "Gangster Disciples" be arrested, calling Kirk's suggestion "headline grabbing" and an "upper-middle-class, elitist white boy solution to a problem he knows nothing about".
A spokesman for Kirk said Kirk had dealt with the issues for decades.

Also in 2013, Alex Clifford was forced to resign as CEO of ___E:Metra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra)___ commuter rail agency, but soon after he left, a memo was released indirectly accusing Rush of using his political power to steer a $50,000 contract to a Washington-based business group.

In the ___E:2015 Chicago mayoral election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Chicago_mayoral_election)___ , Rush endorsed Mayor ___E:Rahm Emanuel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahm_Emanuel)___ in Emanuel's runoff reelection campaign against ___E:Jesus "Chuy" Garcia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus_%22Chuy%22_Garcia)___ .

In the ___E:2019 Chicago mayoral election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Chicago_mayoral_election)___ , Rush endorsed ___E:Bill Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_M._Daley)___ in the first round  and ___E:Toni Preckwinkle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Preckwinkle)___ in the runoff.

Though a very close friend of former President ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ and his wife, ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ , Rush announced early on in the ___E:2008 Democratic primaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries,_2008)___ that he would support Obama.

After Obama won the presidency and vacated his Senate seat, Rush said that an African American should be appointed to the seat:  "With the resignation of President-elect Obama, we now have no African-Americans in the ___E:United States Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate)___ , and we believe it will be a national disgrace to not have this seat filled by one of the many capable African-American Illinois politicians."  Rush said he did not support any particular person and was not interested in the seat.   On December 30, 2008, Governor ___E:Rod Blagojevich U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Blagojevich)___ announced his appointment of ___E:Roland Burris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roland_Burris)___ , the former ___E:Attorney General of Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attorney_General_of_Illinois)___ ; Rush was present at the press conference and spoke in support of Burris.
Rush endorsed ___E:Kamala Harris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamala_Harris)___ in the 2020 Democratic presidential primary.
After she dropped out, he endorsed ___E:Michael Bloomberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bloomberg)___ and became his campaign's national co-chair.

Rush endorsed incumbent ___E:Lori Lightfoot U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lori_Lightfoot)___ in the ___E:2023 Chicago mayoral election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Chicago_mayoral_election)___ .

After Lightfoot failed to advance to the runoff, Rush endorsed ___E:Paul Vallas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Vallas)___ , who was backed by Chicago's ___E:Fraternal Order of Police U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraternal_Order_of_Police)___ .
Vallas lost to progressive Cook County Commissioner ___E:Brandon Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandon_Johnson)___ .

Rush had been considered a loyal Democrat during his tenure; in the ___E:110th Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/110th_United_States_Congress)___ , he voted with his party 97.8% of the time.  Rush was a member of the ___E:Congressional Black Caucus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_Black_Caucus)___  and the ___E:House Baltic Caucus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Baltic_Caucus)___ .

Rush initiated the Chicago Partnership for the Earned Income Tax Credit, an ongoing program designed to help low-income working Chicago residents receive the ___E:Earned Income Tax Credit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earned_Income_Tax_Credit)___ , a ___E:federal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxation_in_the_United_States)___ ___E:income tax U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Income_tax_in_the_United_States)___ ___E:credit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tax_credit)___ .

Rush sponsored the Nursing Relief for Disadvantaged Areas Act passed in 1999. The law temporarily addressed the nursing shortage by providing non-immigrant visas for qualified foreign nurses in Chicago's ___E:Englewood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Englewood,_Chicago)___ neighborhood and was reauthorized in 2005.  Rush sponsored the Melanie Blocker-Stokes Postpartum Depression Research and Care Act, named for a Chicago native who jumped to her death from a 12th-story window due to ___E:postpartum depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postpartum_depression)___ .
The bill would provide for research on postpartum depression and psychosis and services for people suffering from these disorders.

The ___E:Children's Health Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children%27s_Health_Act)___ , passed in 2000, incorporated Rush's Urban Asthma Reduction Act of 1999, amending the Preventive Health and Health Services Block Grant program and including an integrated approach to ___E:asthma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asthma)___ management.
Rush was very outspoken against the GOP's No More Solyndras Bill, which would override a loan guarantee by the Energy Department to encourage research and development.

The Energy Department provided a federal loan guarantee to the solar manufacturing company Solyndra to help with R&D.  He said the No More Solyndras Bill would be better named the No More Innovation Bill.

Rush introduced Blair Holt's Firearm Licensing and Record of Sale Act of 2009 on January 6, 2009. The bill would require all owners of handguns and semiautomatic firearms to register for a federal firearms license.
All sales of the subject firearms would have to go through a licensed dealer.
It would also make it illegal not to register as an owner of a firearm.

On July 15, 2004, Rush became the second sitting ___E:member of Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_Congress)___ , after ___E:Charles Rangel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_B._Rangel)___ and before ___E:Joe Hoeffel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hoeffel)___ , to be arrested for ___E:trespassing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trespassing)___ while protesting the ___E:genocide in Darfur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Darfur)___ and other violations of ___E:human rights in Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_in_Sudan)___ in front of the ___E:Sudanese Embassy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_missions_of_Sudan#North_America)___ .

On February 13, 2007, Rush opposed ___E:President U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_President)___ ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ 's proposed 20,000-serviceman troop surge in Iraq. He said the troops' presence in Iraq was the greatest catalyst of violence there and advocated a political resolution of the situation.
Rush said the troop surge would serve only to make the Iraqi situation more volatile.

On March 28, 2012, Rush addressed the House while wearing a ___E:hoodie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoodie)___ in honor of ___E:Trayvon Martin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trayvon_Martin)___ , a teenager who was shot in Florida by a local resident.
He spoke against ___E:racial profiling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_profiling)___ .
As the House forbids its members from wearing headgear as a breach of decorum, Rush was called out of order and escorted from the chamber.

Rush twice introduced the ___E:Emmett Till Antilynching Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmett_Till_Antilynching_Act)___ (named for Chicago teenager ___E:Emmett Till U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmett_Till)___ ) to make ___E:lynching U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynching_in_the_United_States)___ a federal crime.
Federal anti-lynching legislation in Congress had been held up for about 100 years, but the Emmett Till Act finally became law in 2022.
In the ___E:115th United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/115th_United_States_Congress)___ (January 3, 2017, to January 3, 2019):
Rush's career average missed vote percentage is 15.7, much higher than the median missed vote percentage of 2.2 for members of the House.

In the first session of the ___E:114th session of Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/114th_Congress)___ (January to December 2015), Rush missed 15.6% of the votes and ranked 12th in missed votes.
He had the distinction of missing more votes than any other member of the House between 2007 and 2015: of 6,906 votes, Rush missed 1,549 (22.4%).
Health issues for Rush and his wife were his main explanations for his high number of missed votes.

The ___E:Office of Congressional Ethics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Congressional_Ethics)___ referred a matter involving Rush to the ___E:House Ethics Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Ethics_Committee)___ in 2014.  The Office of Congressional Ethics report found he did not pay about $365,000 in rent for longtime use of an office to conduct politics.
Rush has paid family members for years in questionable practices.
He had a family member who for years worked for his church but was paid by a campaign supporter and friend.

The ___E:Federal Election Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Election_Commission)___ questioned a Rush campaign-finance report that showed thousands of dollars spent on vague categories such as "campaign visibility" and "services rendered." His campaign paid his wife, Carolyn, $50,000 in 2015 for consulting, and his brother, Marlon Rush of Lansing, $13,000 in 2016 for two months' work as campaign manager, according to FEC reports.

Oxford Media Group Inc., an Oak Brook company owned by multimillionaire businessman Joseph Stroud, paid the ___E:Commonwealth Edison U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Edison)___ bill—which was well past due, totaling $17,900 for Rush's Beloved Community Christian Church in 2010. Rush had personally been named in a ComEd lawsuit over the church's previous unpaid bills.

Stroud was trying to break into the wireless phone industry dominated by Verizon and AT&T, and Rush was pushing for federal tax incentives that would give one of Stroud's other companies a leg up as a minority-owned business.
A nonprofit Rush started got $1 million from the charitable arm of what is now AT&T for what turned out to be a failed effort to create a "technology center" in Englewood.
At the time, the telecom giant was seeking support for legislation in a House committee of which Rush was a key member.
From 2001 to 2013, businesses counting on favorable actions by Rush in Congress donated roughly $1.7 million to his pet charities.

Rush attracted more charitable corporate giving than any other Illinois congressman by a large margin, according to a Sunlight Foundation study of expenditures from 2009 to 2011. While it is impossible to assign cause and effect, at critical junctures Rush parted with fellow liberal Democrats in Congress to take pro-industry positions aligned with corporate benefactors SBC/AT&T, Comcast and ComEd.
Rush is pastor of the Beloved Community Christian Church in Chicago's Englewood neighborhood.

Leaders of other Englewood nonprofit organizations complained that the church's programs—a community development corporation Rebirth of Englewood, a public health center, and a group serving teens convicted of crimes—received inordinate government aid and weighed heavily on their own efforts for renewal.

In 2013, Rush and his wife, the Beloved Community Christian Church of which Rush is pastor, and another nonprofit organization operating out of the church had tax delinquencies totaling $195,000, and the pattern of tax delinquency was a decade old. Unpaid taxes included property taxes, income taxes, and employee withholding taxes.

New City Bank sued Rush and his wife for $500,000, claiming they failed to pay their property taxes in 2009.   In 1994, Rush owed the IRS $55,000 in federal income taxes, according to Cook County records.
Since 2018, 15% of Rush's congressional salary has been garnished to repay more than $1 million he owes on a delinquent loan for the now-closed church he founded in Chicago.

Cook County Circuit Judge Alexander White ordered Rush to repay the $550,000 loan that New City Bank granted him and seven other co-signers in 2005. With the money, Rush bought the former Our Redeemer Lutheran Church in Englewood and restyled it as the Beloved Community Church of God in Christ.
Rush has been married three times.
His first marriage, when he was 19, was to Sandra Milan.

They had two children together  and divorced in 1973.  He was married to community organizer, precinct captain, and political strategist Carolyn Thomas from 1980 or 1981 until her death from ___E:congestive heart failure U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congestive_heart_failure)___ on March 13, 2017.   Their ___E:blended family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blended_family)___ had seven surviving children at the time of her death.
On June 30, 2018, Rush married minister and author Paulette Holloway.

Rush's son Huey Rich was murdered on the South Side of Chicago at age 29, in October 1999.    He was named after Black Panther co-founder ___E:Huey P. Newton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huey_P._Newton)___ .
Rich's mother was Saundra Rich, whom Rush never married.
On October 18, 1999, Rich was approached outside his apartment building by Leo Foster and Darcell Prince, who falsely claimed to be police officers.

They wore ___E:bulletproof vests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulletproof_vest)___ , and carried ___E:walkie-talkies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walkie-talkie)___ , guns, and badges, but Rich didn't believe them and ran.   Foster and Prince chased and shot Rich, then stole several hundred dollars and keys from his pockets.

He died in the hospital four days later from extensive blood loss.  Foster told police that he and Prince were coming to collect $110,000 worth of cocaine that Rich had been paid to procure but hadn't delivered.
Rich's friends didn't believe Foster's story, with some suggesting it may have been a case of mistaken identity.
Rush said Rich "was involved in positive—as far as I know—endeavors", adding "as parents, we don't always know".
Foster was sentenced to 60 years in prison for the murder and Prince to 50 years.
The murder prompted Rush to prioritize efforts to reduce gun violence.
In 2008, Rush had a rare type of ___E:malignant tumor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer)___ removed from his ___E:salivary gland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salivary_gland)___ .
He is a member of ___E:Iota Phi Theta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iota_Phi_Theta)___ fraternity.

According to a DNA analysis conducted under the auspices of the TV program Know Your Heritage, he is descended mainly from the ___E:Ashanti people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashanti_people)___ of ___E:Ghana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana)___ .
Rush attributed his election to Congress to ___E:Tony Robbins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Robbins)___ .

His heroes include ___E:Abraham Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln)___ , ___E:Kit Carson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kit_Carson)___ , and ___E:Huey P. Newton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huey_P._Newton)___ .

In 2018, Rush's son Flynn Rush unsuccessfully ran for a seat in the ___E:Illinois House of Representatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_House_of_Representatives)___ , losing in the Democratic primary to ___E:Curtis Tarver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curtis_Tarver)___ .
